term: two-stage acquisition of a reason-signal response selector
definition: Acquisition is a Boolean function of review and external-setting inputs. selfReview copies review, externalBypass copies external setting. record uses its output as the existing ChoiceContext.History law field and separately records a reason-signal preference and imposed constraint; run uses the exact old action function. The inputs are toy mechanism interpretations, not autonomous agents or independently established causal variables. SignalSensitive requires different actions for the two reason-signal values at every fixed acquisition input when imposed=false; it is not correct appreciation of rational reasons.
